commands.summary: List every command with its signature and an example. Offline.
Create an issue of any type. Checks the project's live create screen and any yojo.yaml rules first, and refuses with every problem listed if anything is missing; nothing is written then.
commands.usage: yojo jira issue create PROJECT --type TYPE --summary TEXT [--description TEXT] [--set 'NAME=VALUE']... [--input FILE|-]
commands.example: yojo --json jira issue create PROJ --type Bug --summary 'Login fails on Safari' --set 'Story Points=3' --set priority=High

global_options.--json: Print the JSON envelope even on a terminal. Piped output is always JSON.
global_options.--base-url URL: Jira, Confluence, or Bitbucket HTTPS root for this call; works without yojo.yaml.
global_options.--config PATH: Use this yojo.yaml instead of searching the current directory upward.

error.fix: Run `yojo commands` and pass one of the listed paths, e.g. `yojo schema 'jira issue create'`.

login.note: A human runs this. On a terminal, `yojo` prompts on stderr and reads the personal access token with no echo. In automation, a human pipes the secret on stdin with `--token-stdin`; a secret is never an argument, file, or environment variable. The credential is stored per base URL, so `--base-url` alone can reuse it later.
login.error_scenario: the only keyring backend is a plaintext file store

error.message: No secure OS keyring backend is available.
error.fix: Use a native OS keyring: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or a running Linux Secret Service (GNOME Keyring/KWallet) with an unlocked session. Do not configure a plaintext keyring backend.

error.fix: Apply each drift check's fix (update yojo.yaml or the Jira configuration), then re-run `yojo config check`.

init.note: A preview: nothing is written. Add `--save` to create yojo.yaml, which never overwrites a file. To replace an existing file, add `--save --replace --expected-sha256 HEX` with the preview's `existing_sha256`. Team aliases and rules come only from `--input`.

data.yaml:
# Drafted by `yojo init` from live metadata. Review it, then run `yojo config check`.
version: 1
jira:
  base_url: https://jira.example.test/jira
  projects:
  - key: PROJ
notes: Nothing was written. Review the YAML, then run the next command to save it.
No team aliases or rules were added; yojo never infers them. Pass them with --input (see docs/configuration.md).

init.error_scenario: no Jira login is stored for that URL yet

error.message: No stored jira credential for https://jira.example.test/jira.
error.fix: Ask a human to run `yojo login --service jira --base-url https://jira.example.test/jira` in a terminal (it prompts for the token without echo), or pipe the token to `yojo login --service jira --base-url https://jira.example.test/jira --token-stdin`.
